title: Atomic quota checkpointing for fanout embeddings with cancelled tool executions
creator: Anika Shah
description: Background: Non-chat endpoints (embeddings + rerank + structured tool invocations) often perform multi-stage work: a fanout to many candidate vectors, local rerank/postprocess, and optional external tool calls (e.g. vector store lookups or enrichment). Problem: we currently charge and window quotas at multiple points without a deterministic per-request provenance. This causes surprising rate-limit hits, double-charging in partial-failure cases, and inconsistent quota consumption across retries/cancelled executions. This ticket defines a design to make per-request metering atomic and idempotent across fanout + downstream tool executions while preserving low-latency for the common fast-path.
problem_statement: Observed issues: 1) Prefetch/fanout embeds are billed immediately; if downstream toolcalls are cancelled or the client times out, users still pay for prefetched tokens. 2) Retried requests can cause duplicate charges when idempotency tokens are missing or not honored across the pipeline. 3) Windowed quota accounting (rate-limit sliding windows) is inconsistent because partial executions update different subsystems asynchronously. 4) Reconciliation jobs are complex and create billing churn and refunds for enterprise customers.
proposed_solution: Introduce an atomic per-request billing checkpointing mechanism: - attach a short-lived billing_ledger_id to every incoming non-chat request (embedding/rerank/structured). - use a two-phase commit pattern for charge finalization:
design_decisions: Billing ledger is created synchronously at request ingress with provisional entries; provisional entries do not decrement customer quota until committed.
Commit occurs at the finalization step (successful response, definitive error, or predefined timeout). Commit will atomically apply charges and decrement quotas.
On cancel/timeouts, provisioned entries are either voided or prorated based on execution stage; the gateway will attempt to void within the same request context to avoid refunds later.
Idempotency: billing_ledger_id is replay-safe; retries with same client-provided idempotency token map to the same ledger and reuse provisional entries where applicable.
Quota locking: lightweight lease tokens prevent concurrent commits from oversubscribing limited windows; leases are short (default 5s) to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Fallback: when the commit path cannot be reached (network partitions), provisional entries are reconciled by an async job with deterministic rules to either commit or void based on logs and outcome signals.
Metrics: expose provisional vs committed charge metrics and a reconciliation-queue lag metric for SRE/finance visibility.
implementation_steps: 1) Add billing_ledger_id generation and propagation in the API gateway for non-chat endpoints.
2) Extend runtime request context to carry provisional charge entries (token counts, embedding fanout counts, external toolcall heuristics).
3) Implement commit/void API in billing service with atomic DB operations (single-row ledger state transitions).
4) Wire commit calls from endpoint finalizers and error paths; default timeout path to void/pro-rate after X seconds.
5) Add short-lived quota lease service used during commit to prevent window double-spend.
6) Build reconciliation worker that scans stuck ledgers older than threshold and applies deterministic rules.
7) Add telemetry and dashboards for provisional vs committed, refund volume, reconciliation actions.
8) End-to-end tests + canary rollout to 5% traffic then ramp with monitoring gates.
infra_changes: Billing DB: new ledgers table with state enum {provisional, committed, voided, reconciled} and idempotency keys.
Lightweight lease store (Redis) for quota window reservation during commit.
Reconciliation worker cluster (K8s job) with backoff and rate-limiting to avoid storming billing DB.
Gateway instrumentation to propagate billing_ledger_id and outcome signals.
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger state transitions (concurrent commit attempts).
Integration tests simulating fanout + mid-flight cancellations, ensuring provisional entries are voided and no quota consumed.
Idempotency regression tests: retry with same/different idempotency tokens and verify single ledger usage.
Chaos tests: partition billing service and verify reconciliation resolves ledgers deterministically without overcharging.
Performance test: measure latency added for common fast-path; goal < 3ms p50 overhead on ingress path.
E2E canary with a subset of orgs (non-enterprise) for 2 weeks with financial monitoring enabled.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No increase in billing disputes for covered endpoints during canary window.
2) Reconciliation job processes stuck ledgers and reduces provisional backlog to < 10 items/hour at steady state.
3) End-to-end tests show deterministic single-charge per logical request across retries.
4) P50 added latency at gateway < 3ms; P99 < 15ms on canary traffic.
5) Dashboards show provisional vs committed charge migration trend and refund volume drops by 80% for test orgs.
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal alpha traffic (billing team + infra) for 1 week. Phase B: canary 5% external traffic with monitoring and rollback automation. Phase C: 25% -> 75% -> 100% with release gates at each step and finance sign-off. Emergency rollback will void any in-flight provisional ledgers belonging to the canary cohort and resume legacy billing behavior via feature flag.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased latency on ingress. Mitigation: keep provisional writes very small, optimize DB row layout, and measure during perf tests.
Risk: Reconciliation complexity leading to billing mismatches. Mitigation: deterministic rules, idempotent reconciliation operations, and finance test harness with synthetic workloads.
Risk: Edge cases with long-running toolcalls > timeout. Mitigation: allow configurable per-route timeouts and prorated commit semantics for long jobs.
